Metabolism is determined by multiple interacting factors—genetics, body composition (especially muscle mass), age, sex, hormonal status, physical activity, and diet—not by any single variable. The claim that intracellular free amino acid supply is the universal limiting factor setting which metabolic reactions occur and how fast is incorrect; amino acid availability can limit specific pathways such as protein synthesis, but reaction rates are governed by enzyme levels, substrate and cofactor availability, allosteric and hormonal regulation, and energy status.  
CONFIDENCE: 95
